t: A midland Anglo-Saxon kingdom that grew from a frontier people into the largest and strongest of the English kingdoms.
Under Æthelbald and Offa (716–796) it dominated southern England, built Offa's Dyke and dealt with Charlemagne.
Wessex broke its power in 825; the Vikings split it in 877, and western Mercia joined the English kingdom in 918.
dyk: Offa issued a gold coin copying an Abbasid dinar, complete with an Arabic inscription, to which the moneyer added the Latin words OFFA REX.
ev: Penda and Cadwallon kill Edwin of Northumbria at the Battle of Hatfield Chase
Penda is killed by Oswiu of Northumbria at the Battle of the Winwaed
Æthelred defeats Ecgfrith of Northumbria at the Battle of the Trent
An archbishopric is created at Lichfield and Offa's son Ecgfrith is consecrated king
Ecgberht of Wessex defeats Beornwulf of Mercia at the Battle of Ellendun
The Great Heathen Army winters at Repton and King Burgred flees to Rome
The Vikings divide Mercia, settling its eastern half
Æthelflæd dies; Edward the Elder takes Mercia into the West Saxon kingdom

f.capital: Tamworth (principal royal residence); Lichfield and Repton as church centres
f.founder: Icel or Creoda (traditional); Penda (first well-attested king)
f.predecessor: Anglian settlers of the Trent valley
